missing_semicolon.name: Missing Semicolon
missing_semicolon.fix: Add a semicolon ';' to terminate the statement.
missing_semicolon.beginner: In C++, statements are like sentences. Without a semicolon ';' at the end, the compiler doesn't know where your instruction stops!
level_0: Expected ';' at the end of this statement.
Statement requires a terminating semicolon before the next token.
Syntax error: Missing semicolon ';' after expression.
Compiler reached end of statement without finding expected ';'.
level_1: Your line never ended. Like a bad movie. Add ';'
Left the compiler hanging. It needs closure. Add ';'
Statement ran off the cliff without its semicolon brakes.
A line without a semicolon is an unsolved mystery.
Ghosted the compiler at the end of the line. Add ';'
level_2: You had one job: press the key next to 'L'.
Transistors ran billions of cycles just to find one missing pixel.
This line is rambling like your uncle at Thanksgiving. Cap it with ';'
Did semicolons get canceled while I was compiling? Put it back.
Even your keyboard is embarrassed by this omission. Add ';'

undeclared_variable.name: Undeclared Variable
undeclared_variable.fix: Declare this identifier with its data type before using it.
undeclared_variable.beginner: You're trying to use a variable that the computer doesn't know yet! You must declare it first, like 'int score = 0;', so memory is allocated.
level_0: Identifier is undeclared in this scope.
Symbol used before declaration. Define with a type first.
Variable has no declaration in the current scope.
Unknown name: declare type and variable before referencing.
level_1: This identifier doesn't exist. You're texting a ghost. Declare it.
Who is this mystery variable? It skipped the declaration line.
You called a name that isn't on the guest list.
Trying to spend memory you never declared in your account.
A variable showed up with no birth certificate. Declare it.
level_2: Summoning entities from the void? Declare it or call an exorcist.
Imaginary variables don't compile in this dimension. Give it a type.
You're treating this variable like a celebrity you never actually met.
Did you forget to introduce this variable to the compiler first?
Zero declaration, pure confidence. The compiler is not convinced.

type_mismatch.name: Type Mismatch
type_mismatch.fix: Ensure variable and value data types match or cast explicitly.
type_mismatch.beginner: You are trying to fit the wrong kind of data into a variable (like words into a number box). Make sure the types match!
level_0: Incompatible types in assignment or initialization.
Cannot convert source type to target type implicitly.
Type conflict: expected matching data types.
Invalid assignment between incompatible types.
level_1: Square peg, round hole, very confused compiler.
These two types speak completely different languages.
Tried to fit text where a number lives.
These types swiped left on each other. Check compatibility.
Oil and water mix better than these two types.
level_2: Forcing types together like mismatched socks on laundry day.
The compiler filed for an immediate annulment on these types.
Trying to shove an entire string into an integer's locker.
Type safety is law here, and you just got pulled over.
These types have irreconcilable differences. Cast or change them.

missing_include.name: Missing Include
missing_include.fix: Add the appropriate #include header at the top of the file.
missing_include.beginner: C++ keeps standard tools in library packages. If you want to use cout or vector, add '#include <iostream>' at the very top!
level_0: Header file required for this standard library symbol.
Symbol definition missing. Include corresponding header.
Unresolved standard function. Add header directive.
Missing header dependency at top of file.
level_1: Ordered cout but forgot to add <iostream> to the cart.
Standard library tools weren't delivered to the job site.
You forgot to invite the header file to the compile party.
Using functions with an empty toolbox. Include the header.
You called standard I/O without dialing the area code.
level_2: Like ordering IKEA furniture and burning the instructions first.
The compiler knows what you want, but you refused to import it.
Expected the standard library to appear by telepathy. Include it.
Your code is shopping with an empty cart. Add the header.
Even the compiler can't compile tools that were never included.

missing_return.name: Missing Return
missing_return.fix: Add a return statement matching the function's return type.
missing_return.beginner: Your function promised to return a value (like an 'int'), but reached the end without giving anything back. Add 'return 0;'!
level_0: Control reaches end of non-void function without return.
Non-void function must return an explicit value.
Missing return statement at end of function body.
Expected return value matching function signature.
level_1: Your function promised a value and just ran away.
Ghosting the caller is rude. Return what you promised.
The caller is holding its hands out, waiting forever.
Function reached the end credits without finishing the plot.
Promised an int, returned pure air. Add a return statement.
level_2: Your function took the arguments and entered witness protection.
Returning undefined garbage is like paying bills with Monopoly cash.
The audience is still waiting for the punchline of this function.
Non-void function dipped out the back door without paying.
Zero return value, maximum disappointment from the caller.

unused_variable.name: Unused Variable
unused_variable.fix: Remove the variable or use it in your program logic.
unused_variable.beginner: You declared this variable in memory, but never used it anywhere in your code. It's safe, but removing it keeps your code clean!
level_0: Variable declared but never referenced in function scope.
Unused variable allocation detected.
Variable is defined but its value is never read.
Redundant declaration: symbol has no usage.
level_1: Declared this variable and left it on read forever.
This variable is sitting in the corner, wondering why.
Allocated RAM just to abandon it immediately.
A lonely variable with big dreams and zero references.
You gave this variable life, then ignored its existence.
level_2: Giving RAM existential dread for sport? Delete this variable.
This variable has zero references, zero calls, zero purpose.
Marie Kondo is staring at this variable with deep disappointment.
Why reserve memory just to leave it collecting virtual dust?
Recycle bin is ready for this useless declaration.

segfault.name: Segmentation Fault
segfault.fix: Check for null pointers, out-of-bounds indices, or dangling references.
segfault.beginner: Your code tried to read or write memory that doesn't exist or is forbidden (like a nullptr or past the end of an array). The OS stopped the program to protect the system!
level_0: SIGSEGV: Memory access violation at unmapped address.
Process terminated due to invalid pointer dereference.
Segmentation fault: attempted memory read/write out of bounds.
Segmentation violation: invalid memory address referenced.
level_1: You touched memory that wasn't yours. The OS has questions.
Null pointer dereference. You called a phone with zero digits.
Stepped outside the sandbox. The OS pressed the emergency stop.
Memory boundary crossed. Security escorted your code out.
Knocked on memory address 0x0. Nobody lives there.
level_2: Raided a stranger's memory fridge and got tackled by the kernel.
Welcome to address 0x0. Population: zero. Consequence: instant death.
The OS slammed the eject button on your process with extreme prejudice.
Diving headfirst into null pointers like it's an Olympic sport.
Kernel panic avoided only by terminating your misbehaved process.

infinite_loop.name: Infinite Loop
infinite_loop.fix: Update the loop counter or ensure the termination condition is met.
infinite_loop.beginner: Your loop never finishes because its condition is always true. Make sure you update your loop variable (like 'i++' or 'count++') inside the loop!
level_0: Time limit exceeded: loop condition never evaluated to false.
Process execution timed out. Check loop termination.
Loop boundary condition never reached within time limit.
Infinite execution detected: verify iteration counter.
level_1: Your loop is in a committed relationship that never ends.
Hamster wheel spinning at maximum speed. Check exit condition.
Time limit reached. That while-loop broke all its promises.
Round and round we go! The CPU had to pull the plug.
The loop condition swore it would terminate, but lied.
level_2: Some say this while-loop is still spinning across the multiverse.
Loop condition is more stubborn than a toddler refusing vegetables.
Your CPU fans just spun up into low-earth orbit. Stop the loop.
Heat death of the universe arrives before this loop finishes.
Socrates himself couldn't persuade this condition to turn false.

division_by_zero.name: Division by Zero
division_by_zero.fix: Ensure the denominator is non-zero before dividing.
division_by_zero.beginner: Dividing by zero is mathematically impossible and crashes the computer immediately. Always verify the bottom number is not zero!
level_0: SIGFPE: Arithmetic exception caused by division by zero.
Attempted division by zero in arithmetic expression.
Floating point / integer division by zero is undefined.
level_1: Divided by zero and opened a black hole in the CPU.
Math itself threw its hands up and left the room.
Cannot split cookies among zero friends. Check divisor.
level_2: Pythagoras just spun in his grave and tripped the circuit breaker.
Dividing by zero? Do you want to rip the fabric of space-time?
The CPU politely requested that you reconsider your arithmetic.

brace_mismatch.name: Brace Mismatch
brace_mismatch.fix: Ensure every opening brace '{' has a matching closing brace '}'.
brace_mismatch.beginner: Braces must always be balanced in pairs '{' and '}'. Count them up to make sure none were forgotten!
level_0: Syntax error: unmatched closing or opening brace.
Expected '}' before end of file or declaration.
level_1: Every '{' needs a partner. Right now, one is painfully single.
Braces having a custody battle. One went completely missing.
Your curly braces are leaning like the Tower of Pisa.
level_2: More unbalanced than an all-nighter powered by quadruple espresso.
The compiler doesn't know where main() begins or reality ends.
Pair up your braces like shoes before the whole thing falls apart.

general_error.name: Compiler Error
general_error.fix: Inspect the syntax on this line and check preceding lines.
general_error.beginner: The compiler got stuck on this line because the syntax doesn't follow C++ rules. Check the highlighted token and punctuation!
level_0: Compilation error at line location.
Syntax error encountered during parsing.
level_1: The compiler stopped here and made a puzzled face.
Speed bump detected on the road to binary glory.
The syntax police flagged this line for a quick inspection.
level_2: The compiler looked at this line and questioned free will.
Even the strictest LLVM optimizers are baffled right now.
Grab some coffee. Let's fix this line before GCC gives up.

general_warning.name: Compiler Warning
general_warning.fix: Review this pattern to prevent unintended runtime behavior.
general_warning.beginner: Your code runs, but the compiler spotted a risky pattern that might lead to bugs later. It's a friendly reminder!
level_0: Compiler warning: suspicious construct detected.
Code compiled but contains potential pitfalls.
level_1: The compiler let this slide, but gave you a side-eye.
A yellow card from the compiler referee. Still in the game.
Works today, might come back to bite you tomorrow.
level_2: The compiler signed off, but it will remember this betrayal.
This warning is a blinking check-engine light for your code.
Passed by the skin of its teeth. Clean it before it bites.

general_note.name: Compiler Note
general_note.fix: Check previous declaration or header context.
general_note.beginner: This is a helpful hint showing where the identifier or function was originally declared.
level_0: Contextual note providing additional declaration information.
level_1: A helpful breadcrumb left behind by the compiler.
The compiler left a sticky note here to help solve the case.
level_2: Free advice from the compiler. Take it while it's offering.
